findings.title: FallbackLocaleList#[] uses SiteSetting during early boot/non-request context
findings.body: FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale, which requires DB access. This initializer runs at boot before the DB may be ready (e.g. during asset precompilation or rake tasks with no DB), potentially raising errors. Previously config.i18n.fallbacks = true used Rails' built-in fallback mechanism without a DB dependency. This change introduces a hard runtime dependency on SiteSetting (and thus DB connectivity) wherever I18n.fallbacks is used, which could break any management task running without an available database.

findings.title: ensure_loaded! accesses @loaded_locales without synchronization
findings.body: ensure_loaded! reads/initializes @loaded_locales outside of LOAD_MUTEX before calling load_locale (which does synchronize internally). This creates a race: @loaded_locales ||= [] can race with the mutex-protected block in load_locale set up by a different thread, potentially overwriting the array concurrently or causing an inconsistent state. All other access points to @loaded_locales are guarded by LOAD_MUTEX; this new entry point bypasses that protection for its own initialization step.

findings.title: Fallback locale loading walks a list and triggers DB SiteSetting lookup on every request
findings.body: set_locale now calls I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!, which internally calls self[I18n.locale] (triggering SiteSetting.default_locale lookup, and array building each time) before iterating to call I18n.ensure_loaded! for each locale in the fallback chain, on every request. Although ensure_loaded! short-circuits once locales are loaded, the SiteSetting.default_locale access and array allocation happen every request, adding needless overhead per request compared to the previous static config.i18n.fallbacks = true approach.
